question: If a discount asks us to share our AI conversations, how do we decide if the trade is fair?
reflection: When people understand what they give and what they get, sharing data can build better tools without costing them their dignity.

one_line: A new top model arrived the same week that a shared outage showed how much daily work now leans on a few AI services.

top_stories.title: OpenAI launches its strongest model, Astra
top_stories.what: OpenAI released Astra, which it calls its most capable model, aimed at computer use, coding and security work, first for selected customers and then paid plans.
top_stories.why: More capable agents that operate computers will change which office tasks can be handed over, so firms need evidence on where people should stay in the loop.

top_stories.title: Three AI assistants went down together
top_stories.what: ChatGPT, Claude and Grok reportedly had outages at the same time, while a cloud provider serving all three also reported problems.
top_stories.why: Teams that rely on one AI tool for daily work need a backup plan, and their habits under disruption are worth studying.

top_stories.title: Meta offers cheaper AI if you share your data
top_stories.what: Meta reportedly cuts the price of its Muse Spark model by about 95% for users who let their prompts and answers be used to train future models.
top_stories.why: Price-for-data offers are a live test of how people value privacy, a classic behavioural question with direct policy relevance.

saudi_lens.text: Cursor now lets coding agents run on a company's own servers, which fits organisations bound by Saudi data residency rules that keep code and data inside the country.

idea.title: What is your data worth to you?
idea.pitch: Run a choice experiment on how much discount people need before they let an AI service train on their conversations, and how clear wording changes that choice.
idea.first_step: Write four versions of a data-sharing offer and pilot them with twenty adults.

idea_kids.title: The sharing scale
idea_kids.pitch: A class activity where children sort picture cards of everyday information into keep private, share with family and share with everyone, and talk about why.
idea_kids.first_step: Draw twenty simple cards, such as a home address, a favourite colour and a drawing.
